abstract: Industrial visual anomaly detection (IVAD) underpins automated quality inspection, yet deployment is constrained by scarce target-domain data, rare defects, and frequent distribution shifts. Foundation models supply reusable semantic, spatial, and reasoning priors for cold-start IVAD, but these priors are not anomaly-aware, and existing studies vary in their assumptions about target samples, auxiliary data, and model adaptation, hindering fair comparison. This survey reviews foundation-model-based IVAD under a deployment-oriented cold-start formulation. We separate target-domain data availability from auxiliary-data adaptation, distinguishing zero-shot, few-normal, and few-abnormal regimes, and organize methods by their role in the inspection pipeline: preprocessing and region-of-interest grounding, structural anomaly localization, and logical anomaly reasoning. We summarize representative datasets, cross-dataset protocols, and evaluation metrics, emphasizing how data assumptions affect reported performance. Finally, we discuss open challenges in scalable deployment, anomaly-aware adaptation, fine-grained localization, logical reasoning, and reliable evaluation.
title: Foundation Models for Cold-Start Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection: A Survey
